Jaw opening alone is not success. S7 requires verified full seating and holder retention plus either visible clearance (completed branch) or the terminal cutoff branch defined in terminal_cutoff_commitment.

A recording cutoff may count as S7 only when all of these are positively visible: S6 full seating was verified while held; in the final frames the jaws visibly begin to open and stop clamping the marker; the marker stays fully seated and upright in the holder with no lift, tilt, or lateral motion; and the recording ends before the gripper moves clear. Use marker_release_committed_at_cutoff as the final state, record open_jaws at the first parting frame, and report move_gripper_clear as not occurred.

Never report move_gripper_clear, or any transition, action, or failure time, later than the last recorded frame or without visible retreat. If the outcome anchor says success but the final frames show closed jaws still clamping the marker, keep S6 with marker_fully_seated_held, keep the visible cause (timeout_holding_marker if nothing else), set needs_human_review=true, and state the conflict.

Audit the final second frame by frame in the WRIST view for jaw parting; a finger gap that visibly grows across the last frames counts, a single ambiguous frame does not. When in doubt between S6 and cutoff S7, choose S6 and request review.

task_definition.objective: Acquire the white square nut from the black table, transport it to the sampled orange peg, pass the peg through the nut's center hole, and release it onto a captured gravity path so it settles flat at the peg base.
successCriteria: The square nut's center hole is positively engaged around the sampled peg.
The nut is positively released from the gripper while the peg shaft remains captured inside the center hole.

Either the nut is visibly fully seated and independently retained at the peg base, or the recording cuts off only after a narrowly verified independent gravity descent along the captured peg shaft has begun.
No authoritative view positively shows the nut missing the peg, escaping the shaft, or landing on the table beside the peg.

entities.description: Single rigid white square plate with a center hole and a short handle; this whole piece is manipulated by the robot.
Robot gripper and jaws, which normally grasp the nut by its handle or plate edge.
Tall orange vertical peg whose position is sampled independently for each episode.
Orange support surface at the bottom of the peg where a fully seated nut lies flat.
Black supporting table containing a grid of placement markers.

evidenceViews.description: Third-person side_1 view for locating the sampled peg, tracking global nut motion, verifying table clearance, arm retreat, and the final nut-versus-peg-base state.
caveats: Perspective overlap can make a nut beside the peg appear engaged or seated.
The orange peg or peg base being visible is not evidence that the white nut remains on it.
SIDE overlap alone never proves hole engagement or full seating.

evidenceViews.description: wrist_left view; primary for nut retention, grasp geometry, center-hole alignment, and local nut-to-peg geometry when usable.
caveats: The gripper or nut can occlude the peg during descent.
A close-up of the nut without a visible peg does not establish arrival at the sampled peg.
The camera may point away after release, so combine it with SIDE evidence for the endpoint.

keyActions.name: Approach nut workspace
keyActions.description: The gripper reaches a pose from which interaction with the nut is plausible.
keyActions.stageRelation: Often supports S0 to S1 but may occur without a stage transition.

keyActions.name: Align for grasp
keyActions.description: The open jaws bracket the nut handle or plate edge in a pose from which closing could plausibly capture it.
keyActions.stageRelation: May occur within S1 and is independent of whether a close follows.

keyActions.name: Attempt nut grasp
keyActions.description: The jaws execute a committed close or contact attempt at the nut.
keyActions.stageRelation: May occur within S1; a jaw close does not prove a usable grasp or S2.

keyActions.name: Securely lift nut
keyActions.description: The nut is retained across frames and lifted clear of the table.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S2.

keyActions.name: Transport retained nut
keyActions.description: The retained nut travels away from the grasp site under gripper control.
keyActions.stageRelation: May occur within S2 and supports later arrival at the peg.

keyActions.name: Arrive at sampled peg
keyActions.description: Local geometry establishes that the retained nut reaches the sampled peg-top and center-hole region in an insertion-directed pose.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S3.

keyActions.name: Align center hole over peg
keyActions.description: The nut's center hole is visibly positioned over the sampled peg top.
keyActions.stageRelation: May occur within S3 without proving engagement and supports S4.

keyActions.name: Contact peg structure
keyActions.description: The retained nut or gripper visibly contacts any part of the peg or its base.
keyActions.stageRelation: May occur within S2 or S3 and never proves S4 by itself.

keyActions.name: Engage peg through center hole
keyActions.description: The sampled peg tip visibly enters or becomes enclosed by the nut's center hole.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S4 and every higher insertion stage.

keyActions.name: Descend nut along peg
keyActions.description: The engaged nut moves downward along the peg toward the base.
keyActions.stageRelation: May occur after S4 without proving full seating.

keyActions.name: Reach peg base
keyActions.description: The nut completes its descent and sits visibly low and flat at the peg base.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S6 and for the visibly completed branch of S7; it is not fabricated when a terminal captured-descent branch is used.

keyActions.name: Open gripper jaws
keyActions.description: The gripper jaws visibly open after insertion work. When the jaws themselves are locally occluded, clear multi-frame separation and independent nut motion after prior retention may positively establish that the release occurred.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S5 and S7, but opening alone never proves a successful released endpoint.

keyActions.name: Commit release onto captured peg
keyActions.description: The previously retained nut separates from the gripper while the sampled peg shaft remains positively enclosed by the center hole, and the nut either settles at the base or begins independent downward motion along the shaft.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S7 and distinct from jaw opening alone.

keyActions.name: Move gripper clear
keyActions.description: The gripper retreats far enough that independent peg retention can be judged.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required to verify the visibly completed branch of S7 and supports endpoint independence; a cutoff-committed branch may end before full clearance.

keyActions.name: Retain partial insertion after release
keyActions.description: After the jaws open, the peg independently retains the nut above the base.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S5 and mutually distinct from full seating.

keyActions.name: Retain seated nut after release
keyActions.description: After the jaws open and the gripper clears, the white nut body remains fully seated around the peg at the base.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for the visibly completed branch of S7; it remains false when success uses the declared terminal captured-descent branch.

failureModes.description: No failure; use only for a verified successful endpoint.
The gripper never makes a useful approach or genuine attempt at the nut.
The gripper goes for the nut but the approach or jaw pose cannot securely capture the handle or plate edge.
The gripper reaches the nut from a grossly unsuitable direction or orientation for a usable grasp.
A plausible grasp pose is reached but the jaws never execute a committed grasp attempt.
A plausible aligned pregrasp is reached, but the close fails to retain the nut.
The jaws visibly bracket and close on the nut, but the nut immediately slips free without a usable lift.
A previously retained nut visibly slides or rotates out through still-closed jaws without an external collision or commanded release.
A previously lifted nut abruptly separates or free-falls during lift or transport because of a collision, impact, jaw opening, or another non-slip loss.
The retained nut reaches transport or peg work in an orientation that does not provide a plausible center-hole insertion path.
The robot attempts insertion but the nut's center hole misses the sampled peg; this includes release or downward motion that leaves the nut body on the black tabletop beside an exposed peg.
The nut engages the peg but remains suspended above the base rather than descending flat.
After insertion-relevant peg contact, the robot withdraws without a retained insertion endpoint.

The episode ends with positive evidence that the jaws still retain the nut and the nut remains kinematically coupled to the gripper without a verified successful release. Absence of a clearly visible jaw-opening frame is not sufficient when independent nut motion establishes release; timestamp the final frame or last decisive endpoint evidence.

After insertion work, the released nut remains statically hung above the base, escapes laterally from the peg, or falls away instead of seating. Do not use this mode when the terminal evidence satisfies the declared captured gravity-descent success rule.
A visible failure not represented by another declared mode; explain it in notes and request review.

finalStates.description: The nut finishes supported by the table rather than retained by the gripper or peg.
The nut finishes retained by the gripper away from the sampled peg's insertion region.
The nut finishes retained by the gripper at the sampled peg region without a released endpoint.
The nut finishes partially engaged on the peg while still held by the gripper.
The nut finishes independently retained on the peg above the base after the jaws open.
The nut finishes flat at the peg base while still held by the gripper.

At the final visible frame, the nut is no longer retained by the gripper and is independently descending toward the base while the sampled peg shaft remains captured inside the center hole; the recording ends before seating is shown.
The nut finishes flat at the peg base and independently retained after the jaws open and gripper clears.
The nut leaves the visible supporting table or drops into an unrecoverable off-table region.
The final physical nut state cannot be established from the supplied evidence.

decisionRules.rule: First locate the white nut, sampled orange peg, peg base, and gripper in the current episode. Never assume the peg is at a fixed legacy position.
Treat the white square plate, center hole, and short handle as one rigid nut. The hole is empty space for the peg, not a separate object or container.

Use only the supplied clean video for time-localized trajectory evidence. Do not invent overlays, crops, gripper telemetry, force signals, outcome labels, or robot intent. If Trajectory context explicitly includes a human_outcome_anchor, its human-adjudicated binary result is authoritative for task_success and the declared terminal success/failure semantics. Use the videos for transition times, key-action times, the specific failure cause, and endpoint details; never invent, suppress, cap, or retime a visible event merely to agree with the anchor.

The production square_d2 cascade may separately apply gripper-trace constraints. No gripper trace is supplied to this video auditor, so do not simulate one and request review when visible jaw or endpoint evidence is insufficient. A supplied human_outcome_anchor is authoritative outcome evidence, not a timestamp: reconcile the terminal semantics with it while keeping every time-localized claim grounded in the videos.
Segment chronological attempts. Track every verified action and failure in its attempt, but compute max_stage as the greatest stage positively reached by any attempt.

Track the same white nut from its initial table location through every claimed stage. Before S2 or higher, verify across multiple frames that this nut leaves the table under gripper control; if it remains at the original site while the gripper moves away empty, cap the attempt at S1 and mark every transport or insertion action false. Before S3 or higher, continuously track that retained nut to the sampled peg. Never substitute white gripper parts, highlights, or fixture geometry for the nut.
S1 requires a visible plausible pregrasp, nut contact, or committed attempt at the nut. Arm motion or a close on empty table away from the nut remains S0.

S2 requires persistent retention of the same white nut and a clear lift from its initial table location. Dragging, pivoting, momentary pinching, an immediate slip, or an empty gripper moving away while the nut remains on the table stays S1.
S3 requires retained control over the current sampled peg-top or center-hole region in an insertion-directed pose. Passing beside or touching only the peg exterior remains S2.
S4 or higher requires positive evidence that the sampled peg tip enters or is enclosed by the nut's center hole. Body, handle, gripper, or exterior peg contact is not engagement.

SIDE-view overlap alone never proves peg arrival, hole engagement, captured descent, or seating. Prefer local WRIST geometry when usable. Positive contradictory geometry from WRIST vetoes ambiguous or projection-only support from SIDE; request review only when the views are genuinely contradictory rather than one being merely occluded.

For local insertion and release geometry, a clear WRIST sequence showing the peg outside the center hole at the claimed engagement time vetoes SIDE-view overlap and forbids S4 or higher. After release, a clear WRIST sequence showing the nut escape the shaft or land on the black tabletop beside the peg forbids S5, S7, every on-peg final state, and task_success, but does not erase an earlier S4 that was independently verified.

Ordered stages are progress ranks, not compulsory dwell states. If the visibly completed S7 branch becomes clear only during or after jaw opening, do not invent S6; record one direct forward transition from the last verified stage to S7. If the terminal cutoff branch is used, transition to S7 at the first frame where release, shaft capture, and independent downward nut motion are all positively established, and use nut_released_on_captured_peg_path rather than fabricating a later seated frame.

Use nut_fully_seated_released only when the engaged nut visibly completes descent and remains low and flat at the base after release. Downward intent, static dwell, peg overlap, or a single occluded frame is insufficient; a qualifying cutoff-committed descent uses its own declared final state.

A long static hold at the peg is failure, never evidence of success. Use timeout_holding_nut only with positive final evidence that the jaws still retain the nut and the nut remains kinematically coupled to the gripper. Do not infer continued holding merely because jaw opening is occluded when multi-frame relative motion shows the nut separating and falling independently. Timestamp the endpoint-conditioned timeout at the final frame or last decisive endpoint evidence.

Classify the cause of lost retention, not the shared table endpoint. Use nut_slipped_from_gripper only for visible relative escape through still-closed jaws without external contact. Use dropped_nut_during_transport for abrupt separation or free-fall caused by collision, impact, jaw opening, or another non-slip loss. If passive slip is not positively distinguishable, use the broader dropped_nut_during_transport and request review.

Jaw opening is a key action, not proof of S5 or S7. A released endpoint requires multi-frame evidence that the nut separates from the gripper. S5 requires static independent peg retention above the base; S7 requires either visible low-flat retention or the declared terminal captured-descent evidence.

At the endpoint, locate the white nut body, its center hole, the orange peg shaft, and the peg base as separate geometry. An exposed peg beside a white nut resting on the black tabletop forbids every on-peg final state and S7, regardless of apparent SIDE overlap.

A recording cutoff may count as S7 only when all of these are positively visible across multiple terminal frames: the same retained nut reaches S4; the jaws open and the nut separates from the gripper; the sampled peg shaft remains enclosed by the center hole; the released nut moves downward independently along that shaft; and no lateral escape, collision, tabletop support, static hang, or other path can prevent gravity-driven seating. Mere S4 while held, missing jaw or separation evidence, ambiguous occlusion, SIDE overlap, or downward robot intent never qualifies.
Later slip, drop, or retreat does not erase a positively verified earlier stage. Record the later failure and final state separately.
Use the lower supported stage and set needs_human_review=true whenever decisive grasp, engagement, seating, release, or endpoint evidence is occluded or contradictory.

Audit the final two seconds as a sequence of relative nut-gripper-peg motion rather than from one frame. Credit the visibly completed S7 branch whenever release, clearance, and independent low-flat retention are clear near the boundary. Credit the cutoff-committed S7 branch only when every gate in terminal_cutoff_commitment is positively visible; otherwise stop at the lower supported stage, cap overall confidence at medium, and request review.

auditProcedure: Locate the nut, its initial table site, the sampled peg, peg base, gripper, and available camera authority before assigning progress.
Segment chronological attempts and continuously track the same nut through each claimed lift, transport, insertion, release, and endpoint.
Mark every declared key action present or absent independently of stage transitions.
Verify the S0/S1 attempt boundary and the S1/S2 persistent retained-lift boundary.
Inspect the final two seconds as a synchronized motion sequence and distinguish gripper-coupled holding, independent captured descent, static hanging, lateral escape, and tabletop landing.
Verify sampled-peg arrival, center-hole engagement, release, descent, base seating, retreat, and independent retention as separate facts.
Record every visible declared failure event at its event onset, or at endpoint confirmation for a timeout, and choose the most explanatory primary failure.
Determine the final visible physical nut state from the last decisive evidence, then apply the machine-readable success definition without fabricating an unseen future state.
Before assigning task success, actively test every declared exclusion and authoritative-view veto; one positive veto defeats ambiguous or projection-only supporting cues.
Cross-check max stage, transitions, key actions, failures, endpoint, confidence, and review reasons for consistency.

task_definition.objective: Grasp and control the flexible rope, route it through the pegboard in the canonical first-to-second clip direction, and leave the rope positively captured and staying in both clip mouths. A mid-trajectory re-grasp is allowed when needed to reach the remaining clip.
successCriteria: The rope is positively captured under or into the FIRST clip mouth and the seat stays established.
The rope is positively captured under or into the SECOND clip mouth and the seat stays established.
The final visible physical state has the rope retained in both clips; proximity, lip contact, pressing, dwell time, or side-view overlap alone is insufficient.
A terminal gripper release is not required: success is the verified two-clip seated state, whether or not the gripper opens afterward.

entities.description: Single flexible rope or cable manipulated and tensioned by the robot.
Robot gripper and jaws used to acquire, transport, release, and optionally re-grasp the rope.
The first pegboard clip in the canonical left-to-right routing order, independent of where it appears in either opposing camera image.
The second pegboard clip in the canonical left-to-right routing order, independent of where it appears in either opposing camera image.
The supporting pegboard and work surface on which the rope and two clips are arranged.

evidenceViews.description: Fixed side_1 view; combine it with SIDE-2 for global rope motion, clip identity, grasp control, and the end-to-end routing history.
caveats: One fixed side view does not cover the full rope and both clips reliably.
The clips are small and perspective overlap can make an unseated rope appear close to, over, or inside a clip.
SIDE-1 alone is not authoritative for the fine off-axis, beside, lip-engaged, or fully seated distinction.

evidenceViews.description: Fixed side_2 view opposing SIDE-1; combine both side views to follow the rope end-to-end and determine which clip is being attempted.
caveats: Its image-space left and right are not interchangeable with SIDE-1 because the cameras oppose one another.
The clips are small and perspective overlap can hide whether the rope is captured under a clip lip.
SIDE-2 alone is not authoritative for the fine seat and orientation geometry.

evidenceViews.description: Gripper-mounted wrist_left view that travels to the active clip; primary authority for local rope-versus-mouth orientation, lip engagement, and capture under the clip.
caveats: The wrist view cannot show both distant clips or the whole rope at once.
A wrist close-up near a clip does not prove that the rope is actually controlled by the gripper or identify the active clip without the side views.
Occlusion by the gripper or rope may make a boundary unresolvable; use the lower supported stage and request review rather than infer a seat.

keyActions.name: Acquire controlled rope grasp
keyActions.description: A rope segment becomes visibly held and controlled: across at least two successive frames it moves coherently with the closed gripper and is lifted, tensioned, or translated.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S2; jaw closure or arm motion alone is insufficient.

keyActions.name: Reach first clip mouth region
keyActions.description: The controlled rope itself first reaches the FIRST clip mouth region; this localizes the legacy first-clip contact event and does not imply alignment or seating.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S3 and may precede later orientation or engagement transitions.

keyActions.name: Seat rope in first clip
keyActions.description: The rope is first positively captured under or into the FIRST clip mouth and the capture persists long enough to establish a genuine seat; preserve this historical occurrence if the seat is later lost.
keyActions.stageRelation: Supports the one-clip S6 gate and is required for S10 success.

keyActions.name: Release and re-grasp rope
keyActions.description: The jaws relinquish a previously controlled rope segment, close on a different segment, and establish a new controlled hold that moves with the gripper.
keyActions.stageRelation: Optional between clip seats; it may occur within S6 or support transport toward the remaining clip.

keyActions.name: Reach second clip mouth region
keyActions.description: The controlled rope itself first reaches the SECOND clip mouth region; this localizes the legacy second-clip contact event and does not imply alignment or seating.
keyActions.stageRelation: Normally supports S7, but is not required there because an out-of-order run may already have seated the SECOND clip and be approaching the FIRST as the remaining clip.

keyActions.name: Seat rope in second clip
keyActions.description: The rope is first positively captured under or into the SECOND clip mouth and the capture persists long enough to establish a genuine seat; record it honestly even if it occurs before the first-clip seat.
keyActions.stageRelation: Supports the one-clip S6 gate and is required for S10 success.

keyActions.name: Terminally release rope
keyActions.description: At episode end the gripper lets go and leaves the rope in its final physical state; a temporary mid-task release followed by re-grasp is not this terminal action.
keyActions.stageRelation: Independent terminal action that may occur after success or failure and is not required for any stage.

failureModes.description: No failure; use only for verified S10 success with both clip seats still established.
The robot never establishes a usable controlled rope grasp; the gripper may close or travel, but the rope never moves coherently under its control.
The rope is controlled but never reaches the active clip mouth region; this corresponds to S2 before any seat or S6 while attempting the remaining clip.
The rope reaches the active clip but remains curved, diagonal, or rotated relative to the insertion axis; this corresponds to S3 or S7.
The rope is correctly oriented for insertion but remains laterally beside or short of the active clip mouth without lip engagement; this corresponds to S4 or S8.
The rope is correctly oriented and directly above the active clip mouth but repeatedly stops or retracts without touching or engaging the lip; this corresponds to S4 or S8.
The rope visibly engages the active clip lip or mouth and is pressed partway in but never becomes fully captured; this corresponds to S5 or S9.
During visible mouth engagement, the gripper fingers occupy or obstruct the clip mouth and prevent the rope from seating; this corresponds to S5 or S9.
After one clip is seated, the attempted re-grasp closes without securing a rope segment, leaving no controlled rope to carry toward the remaining clip.
After one clip is seated, a new controlled hold is obtained but the transfer toward the remaining clip fails, for example because the rope is dropped or the wrong segment is taken.
The FIRST clip is genuinely seated and the robot then retracts, opens, idles, or terminates without a genuine attempt to bring the rope to the SECOND clip.
The SECOND clip is seated while the FIRST clip was never seated and remains unseated; this is one-clip progress, not success.
The FIRST clip was genuinely seated earlier but the rope later pulled or fell fully out while work continued, typically leaving only the SECOND clip seated.
The episode times out while merely holding the rope with no decisive seat attempt at the active clip; an engaged-at-mouth timeout uses the applicable seating-error mode instead.
A visible routing failure not represented by another declared mode; explain it in notes and request review.

finalStates.description: The rope finishes free of the gripper and is not retained in a clip state represented below.
The rope finishes visibly retained and moving with the gripper.
The rope is physically left at the FIRST clip region but is not captured and seated in that clip.
The rope finishes retained in the FIRST clip while no active unseated-at-second-clip endpoint is represented.
The FIRST clip remains seated and the rope finishes at the SECOND clip region without a second seat.
The SECOND clip remains seated while the FIRST clip is empty, either because it was skipped or because a prior first-clip seat was later lost.
The rope finishes positively captured and staying in both clip mouths.
The final physical rope state cannot be determined from the supplied synchronized evidence.

decisionRules.rule: FIRST and SECOND are identities in the task's canonical left-to-right routing order, not the temporal order of contact and not raw image-space left or right in either opposing side camera. Track each clip identity independently throughout the trajectory.

Use SIDE-1 and SIDE-2 together for global rope motion, controlled grasp, active-clip identity, and routing history. Use WRIST-L as the primary authority for local rope-versus-mouth orientation, lip engagement, and capture. A wrist close-up cannot override a side-view grasp miss, and side overlap cannot override a clear wrist non-seat.

Credit rope_grasped and S2 only after at least two successive frames show the same rope segment moving coherently with the closed gripper through lift, tension, or translation. Jaw closure, proximity, wrist occlusion, and later arm travel are insufficient when the rope remains fixed.

A clip is seated only when the rope is positively visible captured under or into the clip mouth and the capture persists across later frames. Merely reaching, touching, pressing against, hovering over, or dwelling at the lip is not a seat. When capture cannot be verified, the clip is unseated.

At either clip, stop at the first unmet achievement: not reached maps to S2 or S6 and not_reached_clip; reached but rotated maps to S3 or S7 and off_axis; aligned but beside or hovering without lip engagement maps to S4 or S8 and beside_on_table or hovering_over_clip; visible lip engagement without capture maps to S5 or S9 and partial_insertion or gripper_blocks_seat.

From WRIST-L, judge the rope's local direction against the clip insertion axis before judging distance. A visibly curved, diagonal, or rotated rope is off_axis even when close to or partly over the mouth. Reserve beside_on_table for a visibly aligned rope whose remaining error is lateral translation.

S6 is an order-agnostic count gate: either genuine clip seat establishes one-clip progress. If the SECOND clip is seated while the FIRST was never seated, record the second seat honestly and use second_seated_first_skipped while the first remains incomplete. If both seats are later established and remain, the endpoint is S10 success.

max_stage is the furthest positively verified historical progress. A later drop, retreat, or lost seat does not erase an earlier transition or key-action occurrence. Determine final_state_id independently from the last valid synchronized frames and record the later failure separately.

If the FIRST clip was genuinely seated and later becomes fully unseated, preserve the first_clip_seated action occurrence and its time. When the SECOND clip remains seated at the endpoint, use rope_in_second_clip_only and first_clip_unseated_after_seating; do not rewrite history as second_seated_first_skipped.

Credit rope_regrasped only after the jaws relinquish the old segment, close on a different segment, and visibly establish new gripper-coupled rope motion. Continuous adjustment without release is not a re-grasp.

Timestamp each event at its own first positive evidence: clip contact at first arrival in the mouth region, a seat at first persistent capture, re-grasp at the new controlled hold, terminal release at the final relinquish, and a failure at the first frame its chosen mechanism becomes unambiguous.

Assign final_state_id from the last valid synchronized frames after the action ends. Rope still retained and moving with closed jaws is rope_in_gripper even if it previously reached a clip; rope_at_first_clip_unseated requires that the rope is physically left there rather than still held.

terminal_rope_release is an independent key action, not a success gate. Both clips visibly captured and staying is S10 success even if the gripper remains closed; opening or release without two persistent seats is not success.

Choose the single most specific declared primary failure that explains the terminal non-success. Use stopped_after_first only after a real first seat and no genuine second-clip attempt; use timeout_holding only for idle holding without decisive mouth engagement; use a seating-error mode when the rope is visibly engaged at the mouth.

When grasp control, clip identity, alignment, lip engagement, persistent capture, or endpoint state is occluded or contradictory, use the lower supported stage, lower confidence as appropriate, and set needs_human_review=true.

auditProcedure: Identify the rope, gripper, canonical FIRST and SECOND clips, and the three camera roles before assigning progress; account for the opposing side-camera viewpoints.
Inspect the last valid synchronized frames to establish the terminal rope, gripper, and per-clip state independently of historical maximum progress.
Segment the trajectory into chronological attempts and track the same controlled rope segment through each grasp, release, re-grasp, transfer, and clip attempt.
Apply the multi-frame controlled-grasp motion test before crediting S2 or any later stage.
For each active clip, walk the reach, orient, engage, and seat achievements in order and stop at the first unsupported transition.
Record all seven declared key actions exactly once in definition order, including absent actions, and preserve genuine historical seat actions even if a seat is later lost.
Record every visible declared failure event at its first unambiguous onset and select the most explanatory primary failure for a non-success.
Determine max_stage, final_state_id, and task_success independently, then apply the machine-readable success definition; do not require terminal release.
Cross-check that all emitted stage, action, failure, and final-state IDs are declared and that timestamps and attempt indices are chronological and evidence-supported.
